doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Meeting Milt Hinton and his slapping
summary: He met Hinton at Michael's Pub; he marvels at Milt's slap technique and stories.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I met Milt at Michael’s Pub in New York, I think it was that time when Scott was playing with them. It was one of his first gigs in New York and I came by and sat in and everything. I think that was the first time I met Milt. It just feels like I’ve known him forever at this point. That would have to be it, I’m sure that was it.

Don’t get me started. He’s ridiculous. I can’t even imagine, the way I feel at 41, making it to his age and traipsing around the world with that big unwieldy thing, and playing the crap out of it like he does. He does things — he does his slapping thing that I know that © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -11-

no one else in history has been able to do, because I know I’ve tried to do it and I’ve showed other people — I show everybody that cares about it. I videotaped it and slowed it down, because it goes by too fast. He does a note, like a slap note and then a triplet slap, and then a note, triplet note [scats]. But he can do it — I saw him do it once when he was 85, like at a tempo like this [scats]. It boggles. Completely boggling. And plus he and Mona are just such sweethearts, just unbelievably great people.
Some people make you feel good when you’re around them.
Oh, get Milt after the gig, some of his stories boy. It’s like a history book just opening up. It’s just amazing. Amazing character.
